title: AI assistance exclusively for Unity coding
author: Doutrinadev
selftext:
Hello.

I'm a long time Unity developer and have not used many AI tools.

If I want to use some AI tool **exclusively for Unity coding**, what's the simple approach?

Is there an IDE like Devin/Cursor that's well integrated for Unity (like VS Code + Unity plugin)?

Thanks in advance.

comments.author: Illustrious-Lime-863
comments.body: Codex works great on a unity folder now. Pretty sure claude code does too. No plugins needed

replies.author: Doutrinadev
replies.body:
Thanks!

Will try Claude Code now. Is it much different than having VS Code + Claude's extension?

replies.author: Illustrious-Lime-863
replies.body: I am not sure if they would be functionality different. If you have a subscription you could test both I suppose. Claude code is it's own fine tuned coding agent that works in the terminal. If you don't like using a terminal then VS code + extension might be better for you.

replies.author: count023
replies.body: They are the same just Claude code can work directly in terminal of ithiut the ide code editors

comments.author: No-Bed-2073
comments.body: I use https://github.com/mflRevan/unity-control-protocol with codex and Claude. Codex has been better at shaders and complex systems , Claude has been better for ui toolkit and networking.

replies.author: wallstop-dev
replies.body:
That seems cool, but it's entire premise is incorrect. Unity can run in headless mode, it's tests can be ran this way, builds can be ran this way, and the other things, like changing materials and moving files are just file operations that don't require Unity-the-UI at all. This has been true for ages.

I'd be a little skeptical when the very first sentence and premise of a tool is full of so much misinformation.

replies.author: TheGrandWhatever
replies.body: Maybe the tool was also made with AI lol

replies.author: wallstop-dev
replies.body:
It appears to be! It has since updated its wording slightly to remove just a tad bit of the misinformation.

Also, I'm not sure why you would use this when Unity 6 ships its own \[official MCP server/Agent package\]([https://unity.com/features/ai](https://unity.com/features/ai)) that appears to do what this tool does, but without sketchy stuff.

Even checking out the tool's \[website\]([https://unityctl.dev/](https://unityctl.dev/)), it claims to enable CI/CD pipelines over... local websocket? Which, I guess, is technically feasible, but you can still just... do CI/CD pipelines with headless Unity. I'm really interested to know who is creating CI/CD pipelines (typically cloud based) that will then do punch through networking to a local Unity install or spin up a local Unity and do this websocket stuff...

Maybe it's awesome and I don't know what I'm talking about! Would love to hear No-Bed-2073's experience v the official package.

comments.author: notadev_io
comments.body: Cursor is king. It understands your entire project, can setup your prefabs, scriptables and scenes and of course handle all your scripts from within its nice and handy user interface and integrated IDE. Plus composer 2.5 model is almost free and a really strong one to work with Unity. I can’t recommend it enough.

replies.author: Cool-Animator-8571
replies.body: Tu peux donner des astuces qu’on apprendrai à la fin d’un projet? Histoire que je gagne du temps car je crée mon premier jeu avec Cursor et GPT+ comme mon 2eme cerveau pour les idées etc

comments.author: Old-Wolverine-4134
comments.body: Reality check - prepare big bucks for anything remotely resembling a game demo. Cursor works pretty well with Unity and it has a good MCP. But it is pretty expensive to work on game mechanics and even more expensive beyond a simple level design and movement.

comments.author: AltusLudus
comments.body: Claude code + unity-mcp on github - works amazing

replies.author: Bratchan
replies.body: Or u can use codex. I use both with it. It's nice

comments.author: Bastion80
comments.body:
I’m testing Unity AI for the first time, and honestly, it’s working better than I expected.

I started building a multiplayer spaceship game featuring resource collection, block crafting, and real-time ship building. So far, everything is working, and it has even generated assets and 3D models.

The ship controls feel good, the blocks work as expected (thrusters, weapons, tools, etc.), ship building is functional, and there’s already a main menu with lobby browsing and hosting. After just one day, I’m already able to play the game.

I’m using OpenAI Codex to audit the project, find and fix issues, and refine the code. It’s still more powerful than Unity AI in my experience, but honestly, I now have a playable multiplayer game with all the core systems in place and a solid foundation to build on.
